subject: Throughput snapshot & burst-modeling — next technical steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@brightedge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput snapshot & burst-modeling — next technical steps

Paul — great to meet today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we agreed on during the discovery so the team can prioritize the tech deep-dive. Attaching a preliminary sizing workbook that I promised from the call.

Key takeaways from today:
- Primary flow: user chat + contextual retrieval on product pages (search -> chat)
- Expected steady-state: ~40 QPS with average generation of 180 tokens per response
- Peak bursts: up to 600 QPS for 90s windows during promotional events (estimated 3–4x traffic spikes, see notes)
- Latency target: 95th pct <= 250ms server-side (end-to-end budget discussed ~350–400ms incl. network)
- Streaming: low-chatter streaming (token-by-token) desired for product previews, but we can accept partial streaming fallback

Asks / next steps we committed to:
1) Redwood: produce a lightweight throughput snapshot with tokens/sec and KV cache benefits — include two scenarios (optimistic cache hits vs cold start). See attached: brightedge-prelim-sizing.xlsx
2) BrightEdge: export a 24-hour sample of QPS per minute and a representative request payload (anonymized) so we can model token distribution
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive w/ infra and SRE (proposed times next Tue/Wed morning PT)

Notes on modeling approach we'll use:
- We'll map user-level QPS -> model QPS using average tokens per request and response, and include prefix caching impacts for repeat product pages.
- For burst windows, we recommend a hybrid reserved + burst pool plan to meet short spikes without excessive overcommit.

I've attached the sizing workbook and the recording stub. If any of the numbers above look off, flag them and we'll adjust before the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments:
- brightedge-prelim-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)
- call-recording-20270422.mp3 (audio, 6.2MB)

Paul / Markus — following up with some technical framing and a few clarifying Qs so our deep-dive is targeted: 

TL;DR: We'll run two sizing runs (steady + burst) and a streaming feasibility check. To do that we need a couple samples and decisions from your side.

Clarifying questions (short):
- Are the 180 tokens per response an average including metadata/context, or the generated tokens only? If you have a breakdown (prompt tokens vs completion tokens) it helps.
- Do you currently use any CDN or edge caching for product pages that would affect the retrieval step latency?
- For authentication/authorization, are there per-request tokens that change the request size dramatically (we ask because header sizes affect throughput measurement in some cases)?

What we'll deliver by the tech deep-dive:
- Scenario A (steady-state): compute tokens/sec and model QPS for nominal load; recommend instance counts and batching settings to meet 95th pct latency <= 250ms server-side.
- Scenario B (burst): model a 90s, 600 QPS burst assuming 30% cache hit for repeated product pages; show cost tradeoffs for reserved capacity vs on-demand burst.
- Streaming check: simulate a 40 QPS streaming front-end with average chunk sizes of 6 tokens to validate end-to-end interactivity.

Preliminary assumptions I'm using (in workbook):
- Input tokens per request: 80 (prompt + context)
- Generated tokens per response: 180
- Downstream retrieval adds ~40 tokens on average to the model context
- Average model latency per token (baseline on our recommended instance): 0.9ms/token unbatched; batching improves per-token to ~0.5ms/token depending on window

If any of the assumptions above are incorrect, please update the sample payload prior to our meeting. I'm free for the deep-dive Tue 2027-04-27 09:00-12:00 PT or Wed 2027-04-28 09:00-11:00 PT — propose a slot and I'll send a calendar invite (SRE + infra + runtime engineer will join).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Throughput snapshot & burst-modeling — next technical steps

Thanks Markus / Monica — helpful recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 180 tokens is the generated tokens only; prompt/context typically ~95 tokens. We'll anonymize and send two sample payloads (search-heavy and chat-heavy) by EOD.
- Our CDN does cache product pages at the edge; however product-specific widgets that trigger the retrieval are origin-hit ~60% of the time during catalog updates. We'll include a breakdown by route.
- No large per-request auth headers beyond a short JWT (~512 bytes) — shouldn’t materially change throughput.

We can commit to the 24-hour QPS per-minute export and will attach the anonymized payloads to the Drive folder you linked. Proposed deep-dive slot: Tue 2027-04-27 09:30 PT works for our infra lead and Priya. Please send the invite.

Also: for the burst profile, can Redwood provide both a conservative and an optimistic cost projection? The procurement team wants to see the difference so they can plan budget approvals.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the sizing workbook.

—Paul
Paul Nguyen
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform | BrightEdge Retail
paul.nguyen@brightedge.com
